question.text: Under Section 12 of the PMLA, as summarised at p.194 of the NISM-Series-XXI-B workbook, the prescribed minimum retention period for (a) transaction records and (b) records of identity, account files, and business correspondence is:

answer.text: (a) 1 year from the transaction; (b) 1 year after relationship end
(a) 3 years from the transaction; (b) 3 years after relationship end
(a) 5 years from the date of the transaction; (b) 5 years after the business relationship ends or the account is closed, whichever is later
(a) 10 years from the transaction; (b) 10 years after relationship end

explanation.text: The Logic: Page 194 of the NISM-Series-XXI-B workbook, summarising the current Section 12 PMLA rule, states (a) transaction records are kept for 5 years from the date of the transaction, and (b) records of the identity of clients, account files, and business correspondence are kept for 5 years after the business relationship ends or the account is closed, whichever is later. Option C reflects both parts of this source-exact rule. The Trap: The 10-year option corresponds to the older p.193 statement about retention from cessation of transactions, which the audit flagged as inconsistent with the updated p.194 rule — examinees relying on p.193 alone could mis-pick 10 years. The 1-year and 3-year options are simple distractors. In the audit-flagged original, the keyed option collapsed the two distinct rules into a single "whichever later" composite, which examinees could legitimately read as inaccurate to the source. Note: The original keyed wording ("5 years from transaction OR 5 years post-relationship, whichever later") merged two separate Section 12 rules into one composite statement, which is not how p.194 phrases them. The stem now asks for the two retention periods separately, and the keyed option states each rule exactly as p.194 does, so the answer is unambiguous.
